description: PRIMARY deliverable: make the HTTP router build its routes FROM the config store instead of hardcoded handler registrations, and mount the previously-unmounted ops endpoints on the same mux. Add a config.Store.ActiveRoutes seam (RouteInfo{FlowID,Method,Path}) implemented on BOTH memStore and PgStore; rewrite internal/httpapi.NewHandler to enumerate active routes and register ONE generic handler per route that lifts every {name} path wildcard via r.PathValue into Ctx.Input; delete the hardcoded `GET /orders/{id}` registration. Add GET /livez, GET /readyz (gated on connect.Registry.HealthCheck AND config.Store.Ping), GET /metrics (promhttp over observ metrics), mounted on the SAME mux. Thread registry+store+registerer through with minimal signature changes; cmd/engine passes the real ones. Unit tests only in this feature (no Docker). This feature is a prerequisite for FEAT-002, which proves the behavior with the FMC demo flows.
steps: Add `type RouteInfo struct { FlowID, Method, Path string }` and `ActiveRoutes(ctx context.Context, env string) ([]RouteInfo, error)` to the frozen config.Store interface in internal/config/store.go. Keep both compile-time `var _ Store` assertions.

Implement memStore.ActiveRoutes in internal/config/store.go: RLock, iterate active[env] (map routeKey->activeRef), resolve each activeRef to its flows[env][flowID][version] FlowVersion, and emit RouteInfo{FlowID: ref.FlowID, Method: fv.Method, Path: fv.Path}. Sort by Path then Method for deterministic order. An env with no active routes returns an empty (non-nil) slice, nil error.

Implement PgStore.ActiveRoutes in internal/config/pgstore.go: pool(env) then a single parameterized query joining active_pointers (object_type='flow') to flows: `SELECT ap.object_id, f.method, f.path FROM active_pointers ap JOIN flows f ON f.id = ap.object_id WHERE ap.object_type=$1 ORDER BY f.path, f.method` with objFlow; scan into []RouteInfo. Use classifyPg for driver errors. Do NOT cache (routes are read once at startup).

Add a unit test in internal/config/store_test.go: LoadSeed(testdata/seed.json), call ActiveRoutes(ctx, ""), assert the active route(s) are present with correct {FlowID,Method,Path}; add an inactive flow version via PutFlowVersion (active:false) and assert it is NOT returned.
Extend the local httpapi.Store interface in internal/httpapi/server.go to add `ActiveRoutes(ctx, env) ([]config.RouteInfo, error)` alongside ActiveFlow.

Rewrite NewHandler in internal/httpapi/server.go: change signature to `NewHandler(store Store, interp *flow.Interpreter, deps Deps) (http.Handler, error)` (it can now fail if ActiveRoutes fails). Build the mux by calling store.ActiveRoutes(context.Background(), defaultEnv); for each RouteInfo register `rt.Method + " " + rt.Path` with a single generic handler built by `genericFlowHandler(store, interp, deps, rt.Method, rt.Path)`. Then mount the ops routes (step below). Return the mux.

Add `genericFlowHandler(store Store, interp *flow.Interpreter, deps Deps, method, pattern string) http.HandlerFunc` in server.go that: computes wildcard names once via `parseWildcards(pattern)`; at request time resolves+pins `store.ActiveFlow(r.Context(), defaultEnv, method, pattern)` (map config.ErrNotFound -> 404 via statusForConfig); builds Ctx.Input by lifting each wildcard name with coercePathParam(r.PathValue(name)); builds the per-request runDeps exactly as ordersHandler did (templatingRegistry + branchingEvaluator + Trace + Log); runs interp.Run; writes c.Response with writeJSON/statusForFlow. Delete ordersHandler and the literal `mux.HandleFunc("GET /orders/{id}", ...)`.

Add `parseWildcards(pattern string) []string` in server.go that extracts each `{name}` segment from a Go 1.22 ServeMux pattern path (strip a trailing `...` on a wildcard if present). Unit-test it indirectly via the multi-wildcard router test.

Create internal/httpapi/ops.go with an `Ops` type holding `reg connect.Registry`, `store interface{ Ping(context.Context) error }`, and `gatherer prometheus.Gatherer` (plus the logger). Methods: `mount(mux *http.ServeMux)` registering `GET /livez`, `GET /readyz`, `GET /metrics`. livez -> 200 "ok" always. readyz -> bound ctx with a short timeout (2s); if reg.HealthCheck fails write 503 `{"notReady":"registry"}`; else if store.Ping fails write 503 `{"notReady":"config_store"}`; else 200 `{"status":"ready"}`. metrics -> promhttp.HandlerFor(gatherer, promhttp.HandlerOpts{}).ServeHTTP.

Thread the ops dependencies into NewHandler/NewServer with minimal churn: add fields to httpapi.Deps — `Registry connect.Registry` (already present as Conns; reuse Conns for HealthCheck), `Store` pingable (pass the config.Store), and `Metrics prometheus.Gatherer` (nil-safe: when nil, /metrics still mounts over an empty registry or is skipped). Build the Ops from Deps inside NewHandler and call ops.mount(mux). Prefer reusing deps.Conns for HealthCheck and the config store for Ping so the signature grows by at most the gatherer.

Update NewServer in server.go to propagate the NewHandler error (return `(*http.Server, error)`), and update cmd/engine/main.go: build a prometheus.Registry + observ.NewMetrics(reg), pass the real registry (as Conns), the real store (for Ping), and the registry/gatherer into Deps; handle the new error from NewServer/NewHandler (fail fast at startup).

Fix all NewHandler/NewServer call sites for the new signatures: internal/httpapi/server_test.go (TestHandlerRouting, TestHandlerConfigError), internal/httpapi/integration_test.go (TestOrdersEndToEnd — will be superseded/kept by FEAT-002 but must still compile), internal/config/configrun_integration_test.go (serveEndToEndFromPgStore). Update fakeStore to implement ActiveRoutes (return one RouteInfo matching its canned FlowVersion).

Update unit tests in internal/httpapi/server_test.go for the dynamic router: TestHandlerRouting builds the fake store so ActiveRoutes returns the `/orders/{id}` route; add TestGenericHandlerMultiWildcard proving a route `/order/msisdn/{msisdn}` lifts {msisdn} into Ctx.Input (assert via a fake interpreter/flow or by checking the resolved input reaches the flow); add TestDynamicRouteAbsent proving a path with no active route returns 404 (ServeMux miss).

Create internal/httpapi/ops_test.go: /livez -> 200; /readyz -> 200 with healthy fake registry+store; /readyz -> 503 with body naming 'registry' when a fake HealthCheck errors, and 503 naming 'config_store' when a fake Ping errors; /metrics -> 200 and body contains an expected metric name after registering observ.NewMetrics(reg) and recording one ObserveFlow. Use httptest.NewRecorder against the mounted handler.
acceptance_criteria: config.Store has ActiveRoutes(ctx, env) ([]RouteInfo, error) implemented on BOTH memStore and PgStore; both `var _ Store` assertions compile.

internal/httpapi/server.go contains NO literal business-route registration (no `mux.HandleFunc("GET /orders/{id}", ...)` and no ordersHandler); routes are registered in a loop over ActiveRoutes with one generic handler.
The generic handler lifts EVERY {name} wildcard in the matched pattern into Ctx.Input by name (verified by a multi-wildcard unit test).
GET /livez, GET /readyz, GET /metrics are mounted on the SAME mux returned by NewHandler; readyz returns 503 naming the unready dep when the registry or store is unhealthy, 200 when both are healthy.

CGO_ENABLED=1 go build ./... exits 0; CGO_ENABLED=1 go vet ./... is clean; CGO_ENABLED=1 go test ./... passes (all unit tests, including the updated router tests and new ops tests); CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./internal/decision exits 0.
findings:
SCOPE CHANGE (mid-feature, per user via parent): the router is now ZERO-RESTART live-resolve, NOT startup per-route registration. Go http.ServeMux is immutable after construction, so per-route registration cannot serve a newly-published flow without a restart; that defeats the config-driven premise. Replaced it with a SINGLE catch-all handler on "/" that re-resolves against the LIVE config store on EVERY request.

FINAL SIGNATURES (later steps MUST match these):
- config.RouteInfo: `type RouteInfo struct { FlowID string; Method string; Path string }` (internal/config/store.go).
- config.Store seam gained: `ActiveRoutes(ctx context.Context, env string) ([]RouteInfo, error)` — implemented on BOTH *memStore (store.go, sorts by Path then Method, non-nil empty slice for an unknown env) and *PgStore (pgstore.go, `SELECT ap.object_id, f.method, f.path FROM active_pointers ap JOIN flows f ON f.id=ap.object_id WHERE ap.object_type=$1 ORDER BY f.path, f.method` with objFlow, no cache). Both `var _ Store` assertions compile. ActiveRoutes is the HOT PATH now (read every request by the catch-all), not startup-only — it is NOT dead code.
- httpapi.Store (local seam, server.go): `ActiveFlow(ctx, env, method, path) (config.FlowVersion, error)` AND `ActiveRoutes(ctx, env) ([]config.RouteInfo, error)`.
- httpapi.NewHandler: `func NewHandler(store Store, interp *flow.Interpreter, deps Deps) (http.Handler, error)` — now returns an error (always nil in practice; kept for signature stability). Registers ops routes then `mux.HandleFunc("/", genericFlowHandler(store, interp, deps))`.
- httpapi.NewServer: `func NewServer(addr string, store Store, interp *flow.Interpreter, deps Deps) (*http.Server, error)` — propagates the NewHandler error.
- httpapi.genericFlowHandler: `func genericFlowHandler(store Store, interp *flow.Interpreter, deps Deps) http.HandlerFunc` (NO method/pattern args now — it is the single catch-all). Per request: store.ActiveRoutes -> matchRoute(routes, r.Method, r.URL.Path) -> on miss 404 -> store.ActiveFlow(ctx, defaultEnv, match.Method, match.Path) pins the version -> lift params via coercePathParam -> run.
- Pattern matcher (server.go, unexported): `matchRoute(routes []config.RouteInfo, method, reqPath string) (config.RouteInfo, map[string]string, bool)`; helpers `matchPattern(pattern string, reqSegs []string) (map[string]string, int, bool)` and `splitPath(p string) []string`. Rule: segment-wise, literal segments must match, {name} (trailing ... stripped) captures; equal segment counts; MOST-SPECIFIC wins (most literal segments; tie-break lexically smaller Path). parseWildcards was REMOVED (ServeMux no longer extracts wildcards).
- httpapi.Deps added fields: `Store interface{ Ping(ctx context.Context) error }` (pass the config.Store; nil-safe) and `Metrics prometheus.Gatherer` (nil-safe; a nil gatherer mounts /metrics over an empty registry). Existing fields Conns connect.Registry, Decide decision.Evaluator, Trace observ.Tracer, Log observ.Logger unchanged. deps.Conns is reused for /readyz HealthCheck.
- Ops (internal/httpapi/ops.go): `type Ops struct { reg connect.Registry; store pinger; gatherer prometheus.Gatherer; log observ.Logger }` where `type pinger interface{ Ping(ctx context.Context) error }`; built via `newOps(deps Deps) *Ops`; `func (o *Ops) mount(mux *http.ServeMux)` registers `GET /livez` (200 "ok"), `GET /readyz` (2s bounded ctx; 503 {"notReady":"registry"} on reg.HealthCheck err, else 503 {"notReady":"config_store"} on store.Ping err, else 200 {"status":"ready"}), and `GET /metrics` (promhttp.HandlerFor(gatherer)). Ops routes are code-registered and WIN over the "/" catch-all by ServeMux longest-pattern precedence (proven by TestOpsRoutesPrecedeCatchAll).

TEST CALL-SITE CHANGES later steps must match:
- All NewHandler calls now `handler, err := NewHandler(...)` with an error check; NewServer likewise returns (*http.Server, error).
- fakeStore (server_test.go) implements ActiveRoutes (returns s.routes, or defaults to the single route from s.fv) and gained a `routes []config.RouteInfo` field.
- cmd/engine/main.go builds `metricsReg := prometheus.NewRegistry(); observ.NewMetrics(metricsReg)` and passes Deps{Conns: registry, Decide: engine, Trace, Log, Store: store, Metrics: metricsReg}; NewServer error is handled (fail-fast).
- integration_test.go (TestOrdersEndToEnd) and configrun_integration_test.go updated to the (handler, err) form with Store: store and Metrics: prometheus.NewRegistry(); they compile under -tags 'integration cgo' (not run in this feature).
- 'wrong method' on an existing path is now 404 (not 405) because the catch-all receives all methods and the resolver finds no route for that method; TestHandlerRouting asserts this.

VERIFICATION (all pass in the worktree): CGO_ENABLED=1 go build ./... (0); CGO_ENABLED=1 go vet ./... (clean); CGO_ENABLED=1 go test ./... (all pass, incl. TestZeroRestartRouting proving publish-then-serve with NO restart, TestOpsRoutesPrecedeCatchAll, TestMatchRoute, TestGenericHandlerMultiWildcard, ops tests, config ActiveRoutes test); CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./internal/decision (0). Integration-tagged files compile under -tags 'integration cgo'. The full zero-restart integration proof against ephemeral postgres is left for FEAT-002 (unit-level TestZeroRestartRouting proves the mechanism here).
